title: Pop Monroe's needle whiskey and jamming in Kansas City
summary: He met Lester before Basie while jamming at Pop Monroe's, where a pitcher of needle whiskey cost twenty cents.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Did you first meet Lester with Basie, or had you known him before?

No, I had met him before. We used to jam, go jamming up in Kansas City. We used to go to a place called Pop Monroe's, Pops Monroe. And he used to sell needle whiskey. They called it needle whiskey. It was corn, but it was cured by needles. And he had a pen up at his house, and we used to go there and play all night long. Several guys. I just can't remember all the guys that used to go. So we'd just go up there and take out a little... I think you could get a pitcher of whiskey for 20 cents, you know. And we'd go up there, and drink and play, and there was a piano player that played for us -- and we'd play. That's the good old Kansas City days.
